title: Better Global ETF: Vanguard's VT vs. the iShares URTH
author: Robert Izquierdo
description: Vanguard's Total World Stock ETF (VT) is recommended over iShares MSCI World ETF (URTH) due to its significantly lower expense ratio (0.06% vs 0.24%), broader global diversification including emerging markets, higher dividend yield (1.8% vs 1.4%), and larger asset base. While both offer similar sector allocations and comparable performance, VT provides exposure to key AI-related companies like TSMC and SK Hynix that URTH excludes.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Recommended as the better choice due to lower expense ratio (0.06%), higher dividend yield (1.8%), broader diversification with 9,773 holdings including emerging markets, larger AUM ($101.7B), and exposure to key AI semiconductor companies like TSMC and SK Hynix.

Presented as a viable alternative but with notable limitations: higher expense ratio (0.24%), smaller portfolio (1,253 holdings), developed markets only, lower dividend yield (1.4%), and lacks exposure to emerging market AI-related companies. title: Invest Like Buffett: Lessons From the Oracle of Omaha
author: Na
description: Following Warren Buffett's step down as chairman of Berkshire Hathaway, the article explores his investment philosophy emphasizing long-term ownership, high-quality businesses with economic moats, and low-cost index funds. Buffett's approach has delivered nearly double the S&P 500's returns over six decades. The article highlights his preference for index funds over active management, focus on companies with durable competitive advantages, and recent increased investments in Japanese trading houses.

title: 3 Reasons to Hold Alibaba Stock Despite Its High Premium P/S
author: Na
description: Alibaba trades at a premium valuation but offers fundamental support for existing shareholders to hold. The company's cloud and AI businesses are accelerating with AI revenues exceeding one-third of cloud sales, core e-commerce remains resilient to fund AI ambitions, and management has outlined a disciplined multi-year AI infrastructure payback plan. While near-term margin pressure from capex and quick commerce losses persists, consensus earnings growth of 76.61% for fiscal 2027 supports patience through the current investment cycle.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Accelerating cloud and AI monetization with triple-digit AI revenue growth for 12 consecutive quarters, resilient core commerce generating cash to self-fund transformation, and disciplined capital allocation framework with defined payback horizon. Consensus fiscal 2027 earnings expected to grow 76.61% YoY, supporting long-term holding thesis despite near-term headwinds.

title: CrowdStrike vs. Palantir Technologies: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
author: Pamela Kock
description: The article compares CrowdStrike and Palantir Technologies as investment options for 2026. CrowdStrike offers a leading cybersecurity platform with 22% revenue growth but remains unprofitable and faces reputational damage from a 2024 outage. Palantir demonstrates stronger financial performance with 56% revenue growth, profitability, and no debt, but carries higher valuation and customer concentration risks. The author recommends CrowdStrike for its better balance between growth and valuation, despite ongoing challenges.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strong market position and resilient stock recovery post-outage, but offset by ongoing unprofitability (-3.4% net margin), reputational damage from July 2024 incident, and slower growth (21.7% YoY). Recommended by author as better value despite challenges.

Exceptional financial performance with 56.2% revenue growth, strong profitability (36.3% net margin), zero debt, high liquidity, and expanding commercial customer base. However, positive sentiment is tempered by high valuation multiples and customer concentration risk.

title: IREN Broadens Its AI Customer Base: Can Diversification Pay Off?
author: Na
description: IREN Limited is diversifying its AI cloud customer base away from heavy dependence on Microsoft and NVIDIA by signing $2.8 billion in contracts with Prometheus, Perplexity, and Together AI in July 2026. The company is experiencing stronger contract economics with three-year pricing up 125% and five-year pricing up 70%, though it faces risks from early-stage customers and shorter contracts. With 2026 capacity largely sold out, IREN is targeting broader customer expansion for 2027-2028.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Company signed significant $2.8B in new contracts, achieved substantial pricing increases (125% for 3-year, 70% for 5-year contracts), and is successfully diversifying customer base away from concentration risk. However, sentiment is tempered by downward earnings revisions and premium valuation.

Strong Q2 2026 performance with $2.58B in revenues and $104B revenue backlog. Demonstrates significant scale with 1.5 GW active power and 3.7 GW contracted power, positioning it well in the competitive AI cloud market.
Solid Q2 2026 results with $582.3M group revenues and $3B ARR. Closed four major AI-cloud deals averaging over $1B each and raised contracted-power target to 5 GW, indicating strong growth momentum.
